request.query: Nonzero image integer absolute value at least one in ordered field polynomial evaluation

content.text:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "one_le_pow_mul_abs_eval_div",
      "informal_name": "Lower Bound for Polynomial Evaluation at Rational Points",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] {f : Polynomial ℤ} {a b : ℤ},\n  0 < b →\n    Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f) ≠ 0 →\n      1 ≤ ↑b ^ f.natDegree * |Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f)|",
      "informal_description": "For any linearly ordered field $ K $ with strict ordered ring structure, given a non-zero polynomial $ f \\in \\mathbb{Z}[X] $, integers $ a, b $ with $ b > 0 $, and assuming $ f\\left(\\frac{a}{b}\\right) \\neq 0 $, it holds that $ 1 \\leq b^{\\deg(f)} \\cdot \\left| f\\left(\\frac{a}{b}\\right) \\right| $, where $ \\deg(f) $ denotes the natural degree of $ f $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.DenomsClearable"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.Chebyshev.one_lt_abs_eval_T_real",
      "informal_name": "Absolute Value of Chebyshev Polynomial $ T_n(x) $ Exceeds 1 for $ |x| > 1 $",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {n : ℤ}, n ≠ 0 → ∀ {x : ℝ}, 1 < |x| → 1 < |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ n)|",
      "informal_description": "For any non-zero integer $ n $ and real number $ x $ with $ |x| > 1 $, the absolute value of the Chebyshev polynomial $ T_n(x) $ satisfies $ |T_n(x)| > 1 $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.RootsExtrema"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.Chebyshev.one_le_abs_eval_T_real",
      "informal_name": "Chebyshev Polynomial Evaluation Lower Bound for |x| ≥ 1",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (n : ℤ) {x : ℝ}, 1 ≤ |x| → 1 ≤ |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ n)|",
      "informal_description": "For any integer $n$ and real number $x$ with $|x| \\geq 1$, the absolute value of the Chebyshev polynomial $T_n$ evaluated at $x$ satisfies $1 \\leq |T_n(x)|$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.RootsExtrema"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.tendsto_abv_aeval_atTop",
      "informal_name": "Absolute Value of Polynomial Evaluation Tends to Infinity",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {k : Type u_3} {α : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Ring A]\n  [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [inst_3 : Field k] [inst_4 : LinearOrder k] [IsStrictOrderedRing k] (abv : A → k)\n  [IsAbsoluteValue abv] (p : Polynomial R),\n  0 < p.degree →\n    (algebraMap R A) p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 →\n      ∀ {l : Filter α} {z : α → A},\n        Filter.Tendsto (abv ∘ z) l Filter.atTop →\n          Filter.Tendsto (fun x => abv ((Polynomial.aeval (z x)) p)) l Filter.atTop",
      "informal_description": "For a polynomial $ p $ with positive degree and non-zero leading coefficient in $ R[X] $, if the absolute value of $ z(x) $ tends to infinity along a filter $ l $, then the absolute value of $ p $ evaluated at $ z(x) $ also tends to infinity along $ l $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Polynomial"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Dioph.abs_poly_dioph",
      "informal_name": "Absolute Value of Integer Polynomial is Diophantine",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {α : Type u} (p : Poly α), Dioph.DiophFn fun v => (p v).natAbs",
      "informal_description": "For any polynomial $ p $ with integer coefficients in variables indexed by $ \\alpha $, the function that maps each valuation $ v : \\alpha \\to \\mathbb{N} $ to the absolute value of $ p(v) $ is a Diophantine function. This means there exists a polynomial equation in variables indexed by $ \\alpha \\oplus \\beta $ with integer coefficients such that for any $ v : \\alpha \\to \\mathbb{N} $, there exists $ t : \\beta \\to \\mathbb{N} $ making the equation hold if and only if $ |p(v)| $ equals the extended valuation at $ \\text{none} $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.NumberTheory.Dioph"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.tendsto_abv_eval₂_atTop",
      "informal_name": "Polynomial Evaluation Tends to Infinity with Input Absolute Value",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {k : Type u_3} {α : Type u_4} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : Field k]\n  [inst_3 : LinearOrder k] [IsStrictOrderedRing k] (f : R →+* S) (abv : S → k) [IsAbsoluteValue abv] (p : Polynomial R),\n  0 < p.degree →\n    f p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 →\n      ∀ {l : Filter α} {z : α → S},\n        Filter.Tendsto (abv ∘ z) l Filter.atTop →\n          Filter.Tendsto (fun x => abv (Polynomial.eval₂ f (z x) p)) l Filter.atTop",
      "informal_description": "For a polynomial $ p $ with positive degree and non-zero leading coefficient, if the absolute value of a sequence $ z $ tends to infinity, then the absolute value of $ p $ evaluated at $ z $ also tends to infinity.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Polynomial"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.one_le_mahlerMeasure_of_ne_zero",
      "informal_name": "Mahler Measure of Nonzero Integer Polynomial is at Least One",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {p : Polynomial ℤ}, p ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℂ) p).mahlerMeasure",
      "informal_description": "For any nonzero polynomial $ p \\in \\mathbb{Z}[X] $, the Mahler measure of the complex polynomial obtained by mapping $ p $'s coefficients to $ \\mathbb{C} $ via the canonical ring homomorphism is at least 1.",
      "path": "Mathlib.NumberTheory.MahlerMeasure"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.abs_isBoundedUnder_iff",
      "informal_name": "Boundedness of Polynomial Absolute Value at Infinity iff Constant Polynomial",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] (P : Polynomial 𝕜)\n  [OrderTopology 𝕜],\n  (Filter.IsBoundedUnder (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) Filter.atTop fun x => |Polynomial.eval x P|) ↔ P.degree ≤ 0",
      "informal_description": "The absolute value of the polynomial $ P $ evaluated at $ x $ is bounded as $ x $ approaches infinity (in the sense of the filter at top) if and only if the degree of $ P $ is less than or equal to zero, i.e., $ P $ is a constant polynomial.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Analysis.Polynomial.Basic"
    }
  ]
}

items.informal_name: Lower Bound for Polynomial Evaluation at Rational Points
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] {f : Polynomial ℤ} {a b : ℤ},
  0 < b →
    Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f) ≠ 0 →
      1 ≤ ↑b ^ f.natDegree * |Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f)|
items.informal_description: For any linearly ordered field $ K $ with strict ordered ring structure, given a non-zero polynomial $ f \in \mathbb{Z}[X] $, integers $ a, b $ with $ b > 0 $, and assuming $ f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \neq 0 $, it holds that $ 1 \leq b^{\deg(f)} \cdot \left| f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \right| $, where $ \deg(f) $ denotes the natural degree of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Absolute Value of Chebyshev Polynomial $ T_n(x) $ Exceeds 1 for $ |x| > 1 $
items.type: ∀ {n : ℤ}, n ≠ 0 → ∀ {x : ℝ}, 1 < |x| → 1 < |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ n)|
items.informal_description: For any non-zero integer $ n $ and real number $ x $ with $ |x| > 1 $, the absolute value of the Chebyshev polynomial $ T_n(x) $ satisfies $ |T_n(x)| > 1 $.

items.informal_name: Chebyshev Polynomial Evaluation Lower Bound for |x| ≥ 1
items.informal_description: For any integer $n$ and real number $x$ with $|x| \geq 1$, the absolute value of the Chebyshev polynomial $T_n$ evaluated at $x$ satisfies $1 \leq |T_n(x)|$.

items.informal_name: Absolute Value of Polynomial Evaluation Tends to Infinity
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {k : Type u_3} {α : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Ring A]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [inst_3 : Field k] [inst_4 : LinearOrder k] [IsStrictOrderedRing k] (abv : A → k)
  [IsAbsoluteValue abv] (p : Polynomial R),
  0 < p.degree →
    (algebraMap R A) p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 →
      ∀ {l : Filter α} {z : α → A},
        Filter.Tendsto (abv ∘ z) l Filter.atTop →
          Filter.Tendsto (fun x => abv ((Polynomial.aeval (z x)) p)) l Filter.atTop
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ with positive degree and non-zero leading coefficient in $ R[X] $, if the absolute value of $ z(x) $ tends to infinity along a filter $ l $, then the absolute value of $ p $ evaluated at $ z(x) $ also tends to infinity along $ l $.

items.informal_name: Absolute Value of Integer Polynomial is Diophantine
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : Poly α), Dioph.DiophFn fun v => (p v).natAbs
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ with integer coefficients in variables indexed by $ \alpha $, the function that maps each valuation $ v : \alpha \to \mathbb{N} $ to the absolute value of $ p(v) $ is a Diophantine function. This means there exists a polynomial equation in variables indexed by $ \alpha \oplus \beta $ with integer coefficients such that for any $ v : \alpha \to \mathbb{N} $, there exists $ t : \beta \to \mathbb{N} $ making the equation hold if and only if $ |p(v)| $ equals the extended valuation at $ \text{none} $.

items.informal_name: Polynomial Evaluation Tends to Infinity with Input Absolute Value
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {k : Type u_3} {α : Type u_4} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : Field k]
  [inst_3 : LinearOrder k] [IsStrictOrderedRing k] (f : R →+* S) (abv : S → k) [IsAbsoluteValue abv] (p : Polynomial R),
  0 < p.degree →
    f p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 →
      ∀ {l : Filter α} {z : α → S},
        Filter.Tendsto (abv ∘ z) l Filter.atTop →
          Filter.Tendsto (fun x => abv (Polynomial.eval₂ f (z x) p)) l Filter.atTop
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ with positive degree and non-zero leading coefficient, if the absolute value of a sequence $ z $ tends to infinity, then the absolute value of $ p $ evaluated at $ z $ also tends to infinity.

items.informal_name: Mahler Measure of Nonzero Integer Polynomial is at Least One
items.informal_description: For any nonzero polynomial $ p \in \mathbb{Z}[X] $, the Mahler measure of the complex polynomial obtained by mapping $ p $'s coefficients to $ \mathbb{C} $ via the canonical ring homomorphism is at least 1.

items.informal_name: Boundedness of Polynomial Absolute Value at Infinity iff Constant Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] (P : Polynomial 𝕜)
  [OrderTopology 𝕜],
  (Filter.IsBoundedUnder (fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) Filter.atTop fun x => |Polynomial.eval x P|) ↔ P.degree ≤ 0
items.informal_description: The absolute value of the polynomial $ P $ evaluated at $ x $ is bounded as $ x $ approaches infinity (in the sense of the filter at top) if and only if the degree of $ P $ is less than or equal to zero, i.e., $ P $ is a constant polynomial.
